best_for: Video editors on Windows or Mac who want a professional timeline for free and can live with 1080p exports and an online account, with paid plans for 4K and pro formats.
description:
Lightworks is a non-linear video editor from LWKS Software Ltd. Over three decades it has been used to cut films such as Pulp Fiction, Braveheart and The Departed, and it has won two Emmy awards for editing technology.

You bring in footage from phones up to RAW cameras, sort it with bins, tags and search, and cut on a multitrack timeline whose trimming keeps sound in sync. It has color correction, effects, titles and transitions, and audio leveling with EQ. Projects save themselves as you work, imports and exports run in the background, and finished videos can go straight to YouTube or Vimeo.

points.title: The free plan stops at 1080p
points.text: Lightworks Free is not a time-limited trial and adds no watermark, but exports only up to 1080p. Create adds 4K export, BRAW and ProRes decoding and NewBlue Titler Pro. Pro adds up to 8K, 10-bit video, HDR editing, ProRes encoding, and third-party audio and OpenFX plugins.

points.title: Prices
points.text: At the time of reading, Create cost USD 20 a month, USD 160 a year or USD 240 once, and Pro cost USD 35 a month, USD 280 a year or USD 490 once, before sales tax. Subscriptions renew on their own until you turn auto-renewal off in your account.

points.title: Account and internet required
points.text: You must register an LWKS account and sign in to use the app, even the free version, and activation needs an internet connection. The Free license expires every 90 days and renews when you sign in again.

points.title: One-time licenses cover one year's version
points.text: A perpetual license does not expire, but it covers only the yearly version you bought and its minor updates; the next yearly version is a paid upgrade. Older Windows versions in this listing help if you stay on the version you own. Each paid license includes a second activation.

points.title: Windows trails the Mac here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 8 versions but stops at 2025.2, while the Mac listing shows only 2026.1.2. Lightworks' own release page names 2026.1 as the current version.

points.title: System requirements
points.text: Windows 10 or later on a 64-bit processor, or macOS 12 Monterey or later on Intel or Apple silicon. LWKS asks for 8 GB of RAM (16 GB recommended) and, on PCs, an NVIDIA or AMD graphics card with 2 GB of memory. The advanced video scopes need an OpenCL-capable GPU.

points.title: Linux builds exist, outside this listing
points.text: LWKS also offers Linux packages (DEB, RPM, Snap and Flatpak) for Ubuntu 22.04, Mint 21 and Fedora 40 or later, but they are not on Flathub and not listed here. On Linux, the advanced transitions, advanced titles, some correction effects and TotalFX are not available.
